overview:
Summer Lee seeks a third term representing this Pittsburgh-area district, which leans about ten points toward Democrats at the presidential level. She enters the general election with a large financial advantage, roughly $1.6 million on hand, while Republican James Hayes has raised about $40,000 and reports under $10,000 in the bank. No outside groups have spent meaningfully against her.

Prediction markets give Lee roughly a 96 percent chance of winning, and no major expert raters have flagged the race as competitive. With no public general-election polling available, the forecast rests on the district's partisan lean, her incumbency, and the lopsided money gap, all of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
